question.prompt: Mika would like to estimate how far she can ride a new model of electric bike on a fully charged battery. She completed two trips totaling \(40\) miles. The first trip used \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the total battery power, while the second trip used \(\frac{3}{10}\) of the total battery power. How many miles can this electric bike go on a fully charged battery?

solutions.explanation:
For this estimate, assume the average miles traveled per fraction of a full charge stays the same. Because both battery fractions refer to a full charge, the total fraction used is
\[
\frac12+\frac3{10}=\frac5{10}+\frac3{10}=\frac8{10}=\frac45.
\]
Thus \(40\) miles corresponds to \(\frac45\) of the estimated full-charge range. To recover the whole range, divide by that fraction:
\[
40\div\frac45=40\times\frac54=50.
\]
The estimated range on a fully charged battery is \(\boxed{50\text{ miles}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Find the distance for one full charge
